paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: how you handle a gift matters as much as the gift. Paul says his team is taking great care "to do what is right, not only in the eyes of the Lord, but also in the eyes of men" (2 Corinthians 8:21). He wants no criticism of how the gift is handled (2 Corinthians 8:20). Giving is about love, and love is worth doing with care.

Now look at the people God uses. Paul thanks God for putting into Titus's heart "the same devotion I have for you" (2 Corinthians 8:16). Titus and the brothers are partners and messengers, sent to help the Corinthians finish what they promised (2 Corinthians 8:23; 9:5). I think that's a gift too. God gives you people who help you follow through, and He makes you that kind of person for somebody else.

And here's the part I love, baker. Paul wants the gift prepared "generously and not begrudgingly" (2 Corinthians 9:5). A good heart and a good plan go together, because readiness is how eagerness gets finished. So don't just feel generous, get your box packed! That's why I keep my ovens ready, and God can use a ready heart, even from a guy who once cost a quarter.
